newsitem.title: FRANCE: New EU parliament leader yet to make mark.
newsitem.headline: New EU parliament leader yet to make mark.

text.p: Ask the European Union's 370 million citizens if they know the new European Parliament president, Jose Maria Gil-Robles Gil Delgado, and most will say "Gill who?"

The Spanish Partido Popular member, who was elected on Tuesday and will lead the EU assembly to its next elections in June 1999, is seen as highly competent and experienced. But he has never made an impact outside the parliament, even in Spain.

The reserved, 61-year-old lawyer from Madrid has been a member of the parliament since 1989, serving on committees dealing with rules, institutions and petitions governing the technicalities and legalities of parliamentary life.
In Spain his father Jose Maria Gil-Robles Quinones is well known for having founded the Spanish Confederation of the Autonomous Right and was a war minister before the 1936-39 Civil War.
Gil-Robles spent his childhood and youth in Estoril, Portugal, where his parents lived in exile during and after the Spanish Civil War, only returning to his native country in 1952.

To that early experience he attributes his European leanings -- during those years his relationship with other refugees from occupied Europe enabled him to learn Portuguese, French, English and Italian.
As president of the parliament he will hold the reins in the closing stages of the inter-governmental conference in which the parliament is lobbying for more powers.

He will inherit from his predecessor Klaus Haensch, a German Socialist, one of the thorniest issues facing the parliament -- unequal salaries earned by deputies from different member states and the consequent abuse of expenses and perks.

He has had a key role in dealing with some of the assembly's thorniest cases, including demands to lift the immunity of deputies like embattled French businessman Bernard Tapie and French National Front leader Jean-Marie Le Pen.
